ranked.headline: Controlled Benchmarks Test Biomolecular Models on RNA, Genomic, and Single-Cell Tasks
ranked.summary: Pretrained biomolecular models are now judged against task-specific and from-scratch baselines under controlled evaluation designs.

ranked.headline: Computational tools standardize and structure spatial omics inference across platforms
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications add quality metrics, alignment, and gene-level spatial statistics to imaging-based and histology-linked spatial omics.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked deep learning models score protein, antibody and ligand binding interactions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers benchmark structure, docking and affinity predictors against reference datasets and classical baselines.

ranked.headline: Read-based algorithms resolve haplotypes in polyploids, mixtures, and repeat-rich genomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend read-based haplotype inference to polyploid uncertainty, viral mixtures, and pangenome graphs.

ranked.headline: Computational methods for spatial transcriptomics QC, integration, and marker selection
ranked.summary: Cross-platform and quality-control tools now address spatial transcriptomics data across Visium, VisiumHD, Xenium, and imaging-based platforms.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools structure, validate, and visualize omics analysis outputs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications describe open tools that standardize, store, and visualize omics analysis results through defined interfaces.

ranked.headline: Phenotype-guided methods integrate microbiome, metabolite and multi-omics data
ranked.summary: Multi-omics studies increasingly need methods that define how layers relate, not only whether they co-vary, to support phenotype inference.

ranked.headline: Perceptron-like computation in genetic and CRISPR circuits under resource competition
ranked.summary: Shared translational resources and ribosome competition now appear as explicit determinants of weights and thresholds in engineered circuit computing.

ranked.headline: Learned shrinkage and Bayesian aggregation refine genetic association effect estimates
ranked.summary: Association analyses increasingly pool annotations, effect sizes, and traits through learned or Bayesian models rather than testing each in isolation.

ranked.headline: Structure-conditioned models now design and score nucleic acid and protein structures
ranked.summary: Atomic-level structural inputs increasingly drive sequence design, energy prediction, and conformational sampling for nucleic acids and proteins.

ranked.headline: Graph, contrastive and causal priors structure omics representation learning
ranked.summary: Recent single-cell and multi-omics items now encode graph, contrastive and causal structure directly into learned representations.

ranked.headline: Reusable representations learned from scarce or incomplete biomedical data
ranked.summary: Pretrained and autoencoder-based models are being packaged as reusable frameworks for imaging, cytometry, and tracking data under annotation limits.

ranked.headline: Simulators and benchmarks expose coverage, mapping, and modification-calling limits
ranked.summary: Simulation-generated ground truth is now used to benchmark variant, methylation, and tRNA modification calling and to tune long-read mapping.

ranked.headline: New computational frameworks for RNA regulation and transcriptome-based marker scoring
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend RNA-seq analysis to editing indices, senescence gene-set scoring, spatial signaling fields and miRNA targeting.

ranked.headline: Force fields and constant-pH MD refine ion, solvent, and torsion treatment
ranked.summary: Classical all-atom force fields overbind monovalent cations to phosphates, motivating ECC-corrected parameters and GPU constant-pH simulation in NAMD.

ranked.headline: New inference methods map fate, markers, and cell types from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Four recent methods formalize cell identity, lineage maps, and marker selection as explicit inference problems in single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes and collision-free hashing for large-scale sequence and taxonomic data
ranked.summary: Growing sequence and taxonomic resources motivate compact indexes, collision-free hashing, and authentication metrics in these tools.

ranked.headline: Interpretable deep models link brain imaging, genotype, and Alzheimer's phenotypes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a methods paper add interpretable, longitudinal models to neuroimaging biomarker analysis in Alzheimer's and brain-behavior research.

ranked.headline: Simplified microbial models fail under strong coupling; motifs enable coexistence
ranked.summary: Recent 2025 studies delineate when Lotka-Volterra and related dynamic models break down and which structural features sustain microbial coexistence.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking genome and transcript calls against validated truth and annotation sets
ranked.summary: Reference and validation resources for genome and transcript measurement are being expanded to cover low-frequency variants and diverse ancestries.

ranked.headline: Complete reference genome assemblies enable haplotype and structural variant analysis
ranked.summary: Telomere-to-telomere and haplotype-resolved assemblies now provide full sequence substrates for variant, annotation and benchmarking studies.

ranked.headline: Variant tools address long-read SV annotation, VUS curation, and deletion filtering
ranked.summary: Recent tools extend population frequency, ACMG criteria, and read-level heterozygosity to sharpen variant interpretation across sequencing platforms.

ranked.headline: Reproducible workflows and curated references refine microbial metagenome profiling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a large gene catalog show analytical standardization extending across prophage, fungal, and cross-domain microbiome profiling.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models for segmenting cells and imputing missing pose keypoints
ranked.summary: Synthetic training data and foundation-style models are reducing reliance on hand-annotated volumes for cell segmentation and pose analysis.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking ML and LLM methods for single-cell and biomedical text data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published CASSIA study test feature selection, explainability, and LLM annotation methods against defined datasets and configurations.

ranked.headline: Learned models decode metabolomic identities, drug exposures, and disease risk
ranked.summary: Untargeted LC-MS/MS and plasma metabolomics now feed automated identification, drug-exposure annotation, and multi-disease risk prediction.

ranked.headline: Learned models turn label-free cell and particle images into quantitative measurements
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair learned models with physical simulation or statistical testing to quantify and design imaging-based cell and particle assays.

ranked.headline: Language models over protein, genome, and DNA sequences for prediction and design
ranked.summary: Four December 2025 preprints extend LLM architectures to protein-ligand binding, drug signatures, prokaryotic genomes, and plasmid DNA design.

ranked.headline: Computational prioritization of neoantigens, B cell epitopes, and CRISPR knock-in sites…
ranked.summary: Recent tools pair tumor neoantigen ranking and B cell epitope prediction with CRISPR knock-in cytokines to enhance CAR T infiltration in solid tumors.

ranked.headline: Privacy enforced within genomic association and haplotype phasing computations
ranked.summary: Three late-2025 items apply privacy guarantees directly to multi-site GWAS, haplotype phasing and released association statistics.

ranked.headline: Curated multi-omics resources refine gene-level annotation and target prediction
ranked.summary: Curated resources now pair heterogeneous omics evidence with machine learning and language-model literature screening to sharpen gene-level annotation and…

ranked.headline: Methods now resolve chromosome conformation, karyotype and active X chromosome
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell sequencing now expose chromosome architecture, karyotype and X activity from low-input or routine data.

ranked.headline: Attribution and mechanistic analyses reveal what trained neural networks learn in biology
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published benchmark test whether interpretability methods recover genuine mechanisms from trained neural networks in biology.

ranked.headline: Stability and criticality constrain whole-brain and excitatory-inhibitory neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply stability and criticality frameworks to link constraints across individual, whole-brain, and microcircuit scales.

ranked.headline: Phylogenomic and mobile-element analyses refine bacterial taxonomic frameworks
ranked.summary: Genome-scale data are being converted into explicit taxonomic identifiers and thresholds, with plasmids implicated in secretion-system diversification.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of regulatory and translational features from genome sequence data
ranked.summary: Foundation models and multi-omics mining now link sequence features to translation, mRNA stability, and codon usage in disease-associated genes.

ranked.headline: Statistical models address coexpression, batch effects and unwanted variation in scRNA-seq
ranked.summary: Coexpression modeling, batch correction and pseudobulk unwanted-variation control are now being benchmarked against explicit statistical criteria.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-level methods resolve HLA linkage, local variants, and crossover estimates
ranked.summary: Haplotype-aware tools now quantify population-scale LD, define local haplotype variants, and estimate crossover frequencies from SNP data.

ranked.headline: Reproducible sequencing maps environmental microbiomes from subglacial to national scales
ranked.summary: Long-term environmental monitoring and national atlases now demand workflows portable enough to compare microbiome datasets across time and habitat.

ranked.headline: Explicit active-site geometry now drives de novo enzyme scaffold design
ranked.summary: Recent generative methods place catalytic geometry directly into new protein scaffolds, with Riff-Diff and RFdiffusion2 reporting designed enzymes and…
